title: Regional failsoft capacity slicing and variant fanout notes
body:
Purpose
This note captures an experimental architecture for a failsoft-first routing/control-plane pattern that lets the platform preserve correctness and latency targets by (a) slicing reserved capacity into policy-driven buckets, (b) selectively evicting or downgrading work in overloaded regions, and (c) fanout to cheaper/shorter-variant model families (and cached summaries) before falling back to full spillover to another region.

Motivation and goals
- Protect high-priority traffic and SLAs for committed customers while keeping overall system availability high for best-effort traffic.
- Avoid sudden cross-region spikes caused by naive spillover; instead apply progressive degradation steps within a region first.
- Make degradation decisions transparent and reversible, with fine-grained observability and audit trails in the control plane.

Key concepts (short-hand)
- capacity slice: an allocated percentage of a region's inference capacity (GPU-pool tokens) mapped to a traffic class (e.g., reserved, premium-burst, best-effort).
- failsoft mode: when a request cannot be serviced at its original quality/variant due to capacity/SLO pressure, we attempt one or more controlled degradation steps rather than immediate cross-region spillover or outright rejection.
- variant fanout: ordered list of model variants (e.g., v1.q8_1, v1.q4_0-fast, v1.fp16-short) that the router will attempt before moving regionally.
- eviction window: a short rolling time window used to decide if lower-priority requests should be preempted or delayed.

High-level flow (per request)
1) Incoming request lands at regional ingress with metadata: customer_tier, route, token estimate, latency_budget.
2) Route decision consults the local capacity-slice table. If slice for customer_tier has free tokens -> serve normally.
3) If slice is saturated -> evaluate failsoft steps in order:
   a) Shorten response target (max_tokens reduction) if routing policy allows.
   b) Attempt variant fanout: try same-architecture quantized variant (lower memory/latency), then a distilled/short-output variant, then a cached/generated summary (ttl-based).
   c) If fanout fails or unacceptable quality -> queue briefly (soft-queue) for burst reclaim window.
   d) If still unsatisfied and request is high-priority -> trigger regional spillover to secondary region. Else if low-priority -> return a graceful degraded response (short stub + suggestion to retry).
4) All decisions annotated and emitted to control-plane event log for later auditing.

Capacity slicing rules (proposal)
- Minimum slices: reserved (for contracts), premium (commitments+SLA), baseline (regular paying customers), best-effort (free/experimental).
- Each slice is defined as: {min_reserve_pct, soft_limit_pct, burst_buffer_pct}. Example: reserved {min:40, soft:60, burst:10} meaning 40% guaranteed, up to 60% before preemption, and up to an additional 10% only for short-lived bursts and only for requests flagged as burst-eligible.
- Slice enforcement is token-based: we count in-flight tokens (approx. token_budget * concurrency factor). The control plane updates counts every 200ms using local agent telemetry.

Eviction and preemption policy
- Preemption candidates chosen by score = priority_weight / (age_seconds + 1) * (estimated_remaining_tokens). Lower score = better to evict.
- Do not evict reserved customer work. Only evict premium->baseline->best-effort in that order.
- Evicted request decision paths: immediate cancel with 503 + contextual retry-advice OR downgrade to next variant in fanout chain if available.

Variant fanout ordering (concrete example)
- primary: rtx-v2-fp16 (full context, high quality)
- q8: rtx-v2-q8_1 (small quality loss, faster)
- short: rtx-v2-fp16-short (same model truncated to 128 max tokens)
- distilled: rtx-lite-q4 (cheaper architecture, lower quality)
- cached-summary: LRU summary store keyed by user+prompt-hash (ttl 5m)

Regional spillover mechanics
- Spillover only performed after failsoft chain exhausted for high-priority requests. For best-effort, spillover is optional and costs are charged differently.
- Regional spillover is limited by an outbound rate per region and a token cap per 1m window to avoid cascading. Default: 5% of region capacity outbound with 1m token cap.
- Spillover path includes model variant compatibility check and implicit quality score estimate; if target region has only lower-quality variants, prefer local degradation over cross-region if latency delta > 150ms.

Control plane interactions and signals
- Local agent emits: in_flight_tokens, slice_usage_pct, average_latency_95, eviction_events, soft_queue_length every 200ms.
- Control plane maintains policy engine with rulesets and versioning (policy_vX). Changes to policy_vX are canaryed on 1 region, monitor 15m before global rollout.
- Decision API returns: {action: serve|downgrade|queue|evict|spillover, chosen_variant:, reason_code:, trace_id:}. This should be a compact JSON blob attached to logs.

Observability and SLOs
- Add specific metrics: failsoft_rate_by_route, avg_degrade_steps_by_customer, spillover_rate, evictions_per_min_by_slice.
- SLOs to track: P99_latency_serve_for_reserved (target), degrade_rate_for_reserved (<1%), cross_region_spillover_rate_for_reserved (<0.5%).

Runbook snippets (degraded region)
- Detect: platform alert when slice_usage_pct > 95% for > 60s AND spillover_outbound_rate > threshold.
- Immediate ops actions: 
   1) Pause non-essential canaries (console toggle).
   2) Increase short-response cutoff for best-effort by 30% (push policy update).
   3) Flush LRU caches where beneficial (to free KV memory for new requests).
   4) If reserved customer calls still failing, trigger manual regional capacity increase (resize pool) or failover per contract.
- Postmortem checklist: annotate control-plane logs with policy_version and event-trace ids; correlate with billing spikes and CIDR-level network events.

Security and compliance considerations
- When returning cached/shortened summaries, redact any PII using the standard PII redaction pipeline. Cached items must be flagged with privacy-level metadata so private customers are never served cached content from public buckets.
- Audit trail required for any automatic quality downgrades applied to enterprise customers; store decision evidence for 90 days.

Open questions / tradeoffs
- How precise are token estimates for variable models? Conservative estimates increase wasted capacity; optimistic estimates increase eviction risk. Need an A/B experiment.
- Should we allow best-effort traffic to preempt premium in emergencies if compensated later? (billing reconciliation complexity).
- How should we score user-facing quality impact (objective metric) when comparing variant fanout options? Human evals are costly; need proxy signals (KL divergence, length ratio, reranker confidence).

Immediate next steps (actionable)
- Prototype a local agent plugin that enforces slices and exports the 200ms telemetry. (Owner: Liam, Ticket: JIRA-PLAT-7982)
- Draft a small policy language extension: allow policy to express "shorten_by_pct", "allow_variant_family: [q8,q4-short]", and "spillover_allowed: true/false". (Owner: Elena)
- Run a 2-week chaos test on a single eu-central region to measure degraded user impact and false-positive evictions. (Owner: Carlos)

Notes to reviewers
- This is intentionally experimental language ("failsoft"). Looking for feedback on the sizing parameters (min/soft/burst) and the eviction scoring formula. Please add comments inline or drop reactions in #platform-routing.
